Meal Prep

 

On Saturday mornings I leave the kids with my husband, head to the gym and then to the butcher where I purchase all my proteins for the week. Then I run to the supermarket to get all the vegetables I'll need. When I get home I'll start the marinades (those little marinade packets at the store are great if you're bored with your flavors or have a time crunch) and leave those in the fridge overnight.

 

Sunday afternoon is when I'll cook up most of the protein on the grill. Usually two or three pounds of chicken and a bunch of brats and maybe some carne asada. I cook vegetables several times a week- a tray of roasted red potatoes and a tray of Asparagus will typically last two days. After I feed my husband, I pack up leftovers for him to take to work the next day (I've started to include a little love note in his lunches- he likes those.

 

Mornings

After I have my coffee, I get the kids up. While they're playing on the floor I make my some eggs for my husband and serve with some sort of smart carb (usually blueberries or strawberries). After he eats I hand him his lunch that was prepared and packed the night before and he's off. Then I throw in a load of laundry and grab my kids and put them in their high chairs while I cook them breakfast. The next couple of hours is playing with them. When they go down for a nap, I put the clothes in the dryer and fold them when they wake up and are playing. If I need to, I'll start a second load. I do at least one load of laundry a day which keeps things from piling up.

 

Afternoons

I make the bed nice and pretty and spray lavender on the sheets- makes the bedroom feel fresh. Making the bed, laundry, and keeping the kitchen clean are the only things I make sure to do daily. Every other afternoon I'll pick something to clean. It could be vacuuming, wiping down a bathroom, or steam mopping the floors. This takes no more than 15 minutes.

 

Evenings  

After the kids are fed, bathed, and put in their jammies my husband arrives home and plays with the kids. While he's with them, I start heating up a protein and sauté some greens w/ garlic. Those pre-washed bags of spinach and kale are great for convenience. Sometimes I'll have prepped a large portion of quinoa- if so, I'll heat some up and serve him supper. We put the kids down and I gather the garbage and he takes it out. Then I clean up from supper and I'm done for the day.

 

Several mornings a week I have someone come in to watch my kids so that I can hit the gym. I also have a lady that come once a month to do deep cleaning but I don't think I'll need her too much longer- we'll see. Long story short, my house isn't perfect and my meals aren't as well thought out as they used to be before kids but they're healthy and it's not take out. There are many areas I could stand to improve on but these are some of the things that are working well for our family and I wanted to share in case it helps anyone else.
